framework.name: Strategic Priority 1 - STRATEGIC PRIORITY 1: Transformative Governance,
framework.description: This strategic priority focuses on respect for rule of law, improved security, and effective implementation of devolution for a peaceful and secure cohesive, equitable and prosperous Kenya. This pillar is the political pillar and the programs and policies herein aim at evidence generation and results based management to improve governance at the national levels for the achievements of the SDGs. The focus is to utilize UNs normative and advocacy roles and provide overall high quality support to accelerate Kenya's progress towards the achievement of the 2030, the MTPII, and the government BIG Four Agenda. This Strategic Result has three outcomes Outcome 1:1 By 2022, people in Kenya enjoy improved governance, access to justice, respect for the rule of law, human rights and gender equality Outcome 1.2 By 2022 people in Kenya access high quality services at devolved level that are well coordinated, integrated, transparent, equitably resourced, and accountable Outcome 1.3: People in Kenya live in a secure, peaceful, inclusive and cohesive society

projects.name: Support to the Nairobi River Regeneration Initiative (NRRI)
projects.description:
Nairobi currently turns its back to its rivers. Some 8,884 buildings are built within 30m of the city’s three main river courses (UN-Habitat, 2015). The city’s rivers are noxious chemical concentrations of raw human, industrial and medical waste, negatively affecting the general environment and the quality of both surface and ground water, killing aquatic life and increasing incidences of disease and associated economic and social burdens. Given that approximately 29% of Nairobi’ residents dispose waste into the river, the level of pollution has increased. For example, the levels of Escherichia coli (E. coli) were incredibly high – up to one million units in 100ml of water collected from the river through a recent study. Standards require that there should be no E coli in drinking water. The level of pollution is further exacerbated by the fact that less than 40% of Nairobi’s 696sqkm is on sewer and as a result of this, wastes from households and the informal settlements that have no public waste collection services also ends into the river as does sewage from pit-latrines and other on-site sewerage-disposal methods. Further, inadequately treated effluent from the Dandora Sewage Treatment Plant (DESTW), burst sewer systems and several drainage channels that gather storm water from Nairobi City worsen the pollution situation of the river.

Project rationale and description: Delivery of safe, adequate and reliable sanitation services in Nairobi, strengthening development control and the need to put in place sustainable measures to protect the natural environment including river corridors and green, and public spaces for increased use by residents is a top priority. Through the project UN Habitat intends to support the priority of Government of Kenya – (State Department of Physical Planning, Ministries Ministry of Environment, State Department of Housing & Urban Development) and specialized agencies such as the Nairobi Metropolitan Services - in the restoration of the Nairobi river system for a better urban and environmental performance, and promotion of riverfront development, and green and public space as levers for urban regeneration and economic transformation. Specifically, the project will support the County Spatial Support Programme under the State Department of Physical Planning and the Public Spaces Programme under the Kenya Urban Support Programme. The project provides opportunities for regenerating inner city neighbourhoods such as the wider Eastlands area, supporting local economies, providing alternative connectivity through a network of green and public spaces and a safe network of walkways and bicycle paths, managing storm water, and creating water reservoirs and water parks.

projects.name: Formulating and implementing the digital solutions for responsible lan management and affordable green housing in Kenya" project
projects.description:
Context of the project: Unplanned urbanization, proliferation of informal settlements and inadequate delivery of housing and persistent poor land management, are contemporary challenges that need to be addressed to significantly transform Kenya into a ‘newly industrializing, middle income country providing a high quality of life in a clean and secure environment’ as envisaged in the Vision 2030. Thirty two percent of Kenya’s population of 47,7 million resides in urban areas and the urban population is growing at an alarming rate of 4.3 per annum. Kenya’s urban poor constitute 52% of the total poor population while on the other hand, the urban areas in Kenya contribute approximately 65% of the Gross National Income making sustainable urbanization a priority in Kenya to achieve its development objectives set out in the Big Four Agenda and the SDGs. Land is the primary basis for investment and economic development in Kenya. It is limited in nature, 68% lack land documentation or tenure security and concerned authorities continue to struggle to put in place measures through the NLIMS to improve its management in a transparent and fair manner. Housing on the other hand is a basic human right but there is an annual deficit of 250,000 units due to affordability challenges, lack of sustainable funding and unavailability of land for housing by many urban poor. 

The proposed joint programme on ‘Digital solutions for inclusive land management and affordable-green housing’ brings together four (4) UN agencies under the leadership of UN Habitat to, for the first time, address the above challenges by, leveraging on their mandates and comparative advantages to collaboratively with communities, government ministries, departments and agencies for bigger impact.

projects.name: Preparation of County Spatial Plans
projects.description:
By 2020, ten years after entry into force of the 2010 Constitution and relevant planning legislation, only one County Spatial Plan - Lamu County Spatial Plan - had been formally approved for implementation meaning that majority of the Counties did not met the legal requirements on spatial frameworks as tools for guiding sustainable investments and development. There is urgent need to support the preparation and implementation of county spatial planning frameworks. The County Spatial Plans have the potential for transforming counties including urban areas into growth hubs by attracting orderly and well planned public and private investment opportunities which in turn creates jobs and livelihoods opportunities improving quality of lives of citizens.   

Against the backdrop of rapid urbanization of 4.3% per annum and mushrooming informal settlements, The State Department of Physical Planning has established two priority programmes: The National Sectoral Spatial Programme (NSSP) and the County Spatial Support Programme (CSSP) that are intended to deliver support to physical/spatial planning endeavors at national and county levels in Kenya. The programmes are vehicles to further the implementation of Kenya’s National Spatial Plan (NSP 2015-2045) that seeks to provide a spatial structure that defines how national space is going to be utilized for the realization of optimal and sustainable use of land and a spatial framework upon which various sectoral plans and policies will be anchored and is a basis for preparation of all other lower tier plans. The purpose of the project is to support Counties to accelerate the development of spatial plans to give the spatial dimension to CIDPs and other development blue prints that are spatially blind. This is critical to ensure no place, and no one is left behind in development undertakings as set out in Agenda 2030 and Vision 2030 of Kenya. The County Governments Act (No 17 of 2012) provides a framework through which the lower-tier plans are supposed to be prepared. Specifically, County Integrated Development Plans (CIDPs), County Sectoral Plans, County Spatial Plans and cities and urban areas plans are listed as lower-tier plans that should be the basis for guiding, harmonizing and facilitating development within counties.

This project will build the capacities of counties to prepare GIS-based and integrated city or urban development plans as required by law. While most counties have prepared second generation CIDPs with sectoral plans currently under review, there is inadequate capacity in counties to prepare GIS-based spatial and integrated city or urban areas development plans that could guide urban and rural settlement development, spur local economic growth and enhance investment opportunities.

The Child Protection Management Information System is a web-based database for capturing, processing and managing child protection services in order to facilitate monitoring and evaluation of child protection interventions in Kenya, inform policy and evidence based decision making. 
CPMIS is a child-focused system designed to: facilitate monitoring and evaluation of child protection interventions in Kenya, inform policy and evidence based decision making; provide access to accurate, timely and reliable aggregate-level child protection data; facilitate record keeping and information management on individual cases of child protection; track vulnerable children longitudinally and geographically to ensure continuity of care and protection, including children in institutional care; and facilitate appropriate information sharing between stakeholders and service providers in the best interest of the child.

projects.name: Support Community re-engineering and and recovery processes to mitigate against the impact of Covid 19
projects.description:
With the continuous rise in infections, COVID-19 pandemic has potential to worsen existing vulnerabilities across Kenya, particularly for the urban poor, majority of who reside in informal settlements and are faced with economic, climatic and natural disaster challenges such unemployment, floods and sometimes evictions due to lack of land tenure security. On average, more than 60% of urban dwellers in Kenya live in slums with the proportion of slum dwellers rising to over 70% in major cities of Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu .  The Government’s public health response to COVID-19 includes a raft of protocols: social distancing by keeping a minimum distance of 1m from each other; enhanced sanitation including regular handwashing with clean water and soap, rubbing hands with alcohol-based sanitizers, and observing respiratory hygiene by covering mouth while coughing or sneezing; and avoiding crowded areas by staying at home.

While the above Protocols are simple and clearly understood, majority of the urban poor have not been able to apply them. With an average density of above 28,000 persons per square kilometer and household sizes of five, the informal settlements are overcrowded, both at community and household levels, making the observation of social distancing difficult. Further, acute water shortages and inadequate sanitation in informal settlements is a challenge making the protocol on regular handwashing nearly impossible. Lack of employment makes purchase of soap for handwashing and the use of face masks for protection against respiratory diseases nearly impossible. These challenges hinder effective COVID-19 mitigation efforts in informal settlements. However, a recent study by Population Council in Nairobi, showed that most people in informal settlements have adopted behavioral changes related to COVID-19 prevention (handwashing, physical distancing and staying at home)  but sustaining the behavioral change will be difficult. Majority of residents prioritized water for drinking and domestic use as opposed to water for washing hands. Income was also spent largely on food items and not masks or soap. These findings, even though are not novel in slums and informal settlements, reinforce the evidence of inequalities and economic precariousness in informal settlements associated with lack of basic services (water and sanitation) and pre-conditions for poor health (pollution, congestion and social stress), irregular informal employment and unemployment. While several immediate activities to aid informal settlements prepare and respond to COVID-19 have been under implementation in 18 informal settlements in 6 counties with significant impact, there is need to build upon the on-going activities to link rapid response to stabilization, recovery and long-term resilience.
projects.outcome: Output 2.8.2 - 2.7.2:  Capacity of Cities and Human Settlements  as drivers of sustainable urbanization, economic growth and social transformation is strengthened

projects.name: Africities Summit 2021
projects.description: Africities is the United Cities and Local Governments of Africa’s (UCLG-A) flagship pan-African event that is held every three years in one of the five regions of Africa. Preparation for next Africities Summit is underway and will be held in Kisumu City , Kenya in May 2022. The theme of  this years Africities is “Transport and Cities: Connectivity, Integration and sustainable health system. The overall aim of Africities 9 is to reinforce the consensus and commitments of the SDGs, the NUA, the Paris Accord on Climate Change and the AU Vision 2063 and to agree on a road-map for the region to “build back better” after the COVID-19 crisis in terms of improved mobility and accessibility in cities as well as better connectivity between cities and countries to improve trade and inclusive economic development across the Africa region. The week-long conference in Kisumu is conceived as a watershed moment at the nexus of sustainable urbanization and sustainable transport. It will strive to leave behind a legacy outlining not only policy recommendations for African countries and local governments to pursue but also clear action plans. Simultaneously, it will also address itself to enhance knowledge and skills of local and national government officials and other professionals from civil society and the private sector to identify and implement new solutions to old problems and pre-empt the challenges while maximizing the benefits of rapid urbanization in the region.

projects.description: The Sector Review Report aims to update the Review undertaken in 2011/12. Its objective is to carry out a strategic overview of the Sector and identify changes that have taken place since 2011. It analyses the Social Protection Sector as a whole: describes how the system has evolved, the improvements that have taken place, and identifies challenges that still need to be addressed. It is, therefore, a backward-looking review, analysing the system as it currently is and looking at how it has evolved in recent years. It highlights both the achievements in the Sector over the past few years and key issues that still need to be addressed. A principal aim of the Review is to provide inputs into the development of a Social Protection Investment Plan (SPIP) for social protection and a National Social Protection Strategy (NSPS). The Social Protection Investment Plan will outline the Governmentâ€™s vision for the Sector up to 2030 to ensure that it contributes to the fulfilment of Vision 2030 and progressively realises the right to social security for all citizens of Kenya that is found in the national Constitution.

projects.name: 3.3.1.6 - 3.1.6 Equip  tea factories with low carbon emission equipment
projects.description: UNIDO in partnership with The Kenya National Cleaner Production Centre (KNCPC) implemented the Low Carbon and Climate Resilient Industrial Development (LCCR) project on low carbon and climate resilient industrial development with the aim of creating awareness and to demonstrate the opportunities and benefits of low carbon growth and climate resilient development in the manufacturing (tea processing) sectors through application of Green Industry (GI) policy instrument and Resource Efficient and Cleaner Production practices and techniques. Specifically for this activity, the project has worked with Kiamokama Tea Factory, one of the factory under Kenya Tea Development Agency (KTDA). The installation of more efficient fans and electronic controls has allowed to ensure the appropriate air volume for specific climate conditions for tea leaves. Technologically advanced fans and efficient blades, from Taiyo Electric, allowed energy savings of more than 30% in average, equivalent to 11,200 kWh of electricity savings at the factory per year. It is equivalent of about 4.5 tons of CO2 saved a year.

projects.name: 2.5.2.8 - 6.2.8 Launch the Social Protection M&E framework
projects.description:
The National Social Protection Secretariat (NSPS) is in charge of monitoring the social protection sector and assess the achievements of programmes with regards to poverty reduction in line with the Vision 2030. The M&E Unit within the NSPS is responsible for coordinating the monitoring and evaluation of the system. The 2017 Social Protection Sector Review II and 2017 Social Protection Mapping revealed important gaps in the M&E implementation across the social protection sector, including the absence of a comprehensive evaluation framework for the social protection system as a whole to monitor the implementation and results emanating from the policy.
The Social Protection M&E framework, recently adopted and currently in use, is based on the three pillars of the National Social Protection Policy of 2011.

projects.name: 2.5.1.8 - 6.1.7 Print and disseminate 2017 Social Protection Sector Review Report and the Investment Plan
projects.description: The Sector Review Report aims to update the Review undertaken in 2011/12. Its objective is to carry out a strategic overview of the Sector and identify changes that have taken place since 2011. It analyses the Social Protection Sector as a whole: describes how the system has evolved, the improvements that have taken place, and identifies challenges that still need to be addressed. It is, therefore, a backward-looking review, analysing the system as it currently is and looking at how it has evolved in recent years. It highlights both the achievements in the Sector over the past few years and key issues that still need to be addressed. A principal aim of the Review is to provide inputs into the development of a Social Protection Investment Plan (SPIP) for social protection and a National Social Protection Strategy (NSPS). The Social Protection Investment Plan will outline the Governmentâ€™s vision for the Sector up to 2030 to ensure that it contributes to the fulfilment of Vision 2030 and progressively realises the right to social security for all citizens of Kenya that is found in the national Constitution.

projects.description: In 2017, the Government of Kenya announced to enrol all citizens aged 70 years and above into a universal social pensioncash transfer scheme.The pension was launched in May 2018, and since then, over 500,000 older Kenyans have been receiving regular pension transfers. Given the size of the pension, and its importance for the further development of Kenya’s and region’s social protection systems, it was considered critical that policy makers are able to review the impacts of the scheme on older people, their households and communities. This information would allow policy makers to understand whether the scheme is having the desired impacts and identify challenges in implementation. Hence, the Government of Kenya, with the technical and financial support of development partners, committed to undertake a robust impact evaluation of the pension in order to establish a baseline for future impact studies.

projects.name: 2.5.1.8 - 6.1.7 Print and disseminate 2017 Social Protection Sector Review Report and the Investment Plan
projects.description: The Sector Review Report aims to update the Review undertaken in 2011/12. Its objective is to carry out a strategic overview of the Sector and identify changes that have taken place since 2011. It analyses the Social Protection Sector as a whole: describes how the system has evolved, the improvements that have taken place, and identifies challenges that still need to be addressed. It is, therefore, a backward-looking review, analysing the system as it currently is and looking at how it has evolved in recent years. It highlights both the achievements in the Sector over the past few years and key issues that still need to be addressed. A principal aim of the Review is to provide inputs into the development of a Social Protection Investment Plan (SPIP) for social protection and a National Social Protection Strategy (NSPS). The Social Protection Investment Plan will outline the Governmentâ€™s vision for the Sector up to 2030 to ensure that it contributes to the fulfilment of Vision 2030 and progressively realises the right to social security for all citizens of Kenya that is found in the national Constitution.

projects.name: Support to urban waterfront planning and development within the Coastal Cities
projects.description: Support to urban waterfront planning and development is anchored in the 4-year (2021 – 2024) Go Blue project being implemented jointly with UNEP and Jumuiya ya Kaunti za Pwani (JKP) in six Coastal Counties of Kilifi, Kwale, Mombasa, Taita Taveta, Tana River and Lamu. The supports the implementation of the Declaration of the Blue Economy Conference hosted by Kenya in 2018. Its objective is to build capacity of institutions and relevant staff in land – sea planning and management for maximum benefits from the blue economy. The project will build information hubs, promote evidenced based spatial planning, demonstrate interventions protecting ecosystems such as sustainable wastewater and solid waste management, protection of mangroves, as well as developing infrastructure that facilitate access to the benefits from the blue economy such as tourism (public open spaces e.g. beaches), fish landing sites etc while creating jobs for women and the youths. The project was launched on 25 March 2021, inception activities have commenced, and project officers reassigned to support project implementation.

projects.name: Support to urban waterfront planning and development in inland urban areas with lakes (pilot project in Lake Region Economic Block)
projects.description: Neighborhood plan that is guiding the regeneration of the lake front stimulated by the resuscitation of the port attracting investment by the private sector was prepared in 2014. The City of Kisumu’s “Integrated Strategic Urban Development (ISUD) Plan”, identified the Lakefront Area as a key asset for the city and proposed its development as an extension of the Central Business District (CBD). Objectives: Plan the land to  a) benefit the city; b) present economic gains for land owners and developers; and c) preserve the local economy that was active in part of the area. UN-Habitat prepared the Lakefront Development Advisory Plan and further analyzed legislation and overall economic feasibility of the areas. UN-Habitat also proposed the formation of Lakefront Development Corporation, a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) that would promote private sector investment and development of the lakefront. The Governor has so far established the SPV.

projects.name: Capacity building for application of GIS in Spatial Planning, surveying and mapping
projects.description: This Training Course for County Planners was developed, jointly, by United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to build the capacities of County planners in the preparation of GIS-based Physical, Land use, Spatial & Integrated Strategic Urban Development Plans building on the recommendations of the GIS Needs Assessment in Kenya Report prepared by UNDP in 2017, as well as previous training activities conducted by UN-Habitat and partners to both the county executives and policy makers . The Training Course for County Planners aimed to strengthen the nexus between planning needs and policy decisions in counties. To this end, the training course will seek to promote better understanding of GIS and planning needs in counties to enable prioritization of GIS and planning needs in the county budgeting processes. This training aimed to enhance GIS skills of county professionals involved in county spatial planning to promote preparation and implementation of GIS-based county spatial plans and operationalization of GIS laboratories for effective service delivery in counties. The participants were expected to practice skills learnt in their day to day activities to improve their county spatial plan work and to eventually make the county spatial plans

projects.name: 2.5.2.8 - 6.2.8 Launch the Social Protection M&E framework
projects.description:
The National Social Protection Secretariat (NSPS) is in charge of monitoring the social protection sector and assess the achievements of programmes with regards to poverty reduction in line with the Vision 2030. The M&E Unit within the NSPS is responsible for coordinating the monitoring and evaluation of the system. The 2017 Social Protection Sector Review II and 2017 Social Protection Mapping revealed important gaps in the M&E implementation across the social protection sector, including the absence of a comprehensive evaluation framework for the social protection system as a whole to monitor the implementation and results emanating from the policy.
The Social Protection M&E framework, recently adopted and currently in use, is based on the three pillars of the National Social Protection Policy of 2011.

projects.description:
The Child Protection Management Information System is a web-based database for capturing, processing and managing child protection services in order to facilitate monitoring and evaluation of child protection interventions in Kenya, inform policy and evidence based decision making. 
CPMIS is a child-focused system designed to: facilitate monitoring and evaluation of child protection interventions in Kenya, inform policy and evidence based decision making; provide access to accurate, timely and reliable aggregate-level child protection data; facilitate record keeping and information management on individual cases of child protection; track vulnerable children longitudinally and geographically to ensure continuity of care and protection, including children in institutional care; and facilitate appropriate information sharing between stakeholders and service providers in the best interest of the child.
